changes_intro: Pull requests merged since Sep 3, grouped by the wave they belonged to. Every one went through an advocate + critic review pair before merge. Today's catalog wave is first: it is the one that changes what you can type into the app.

waves.name: Catalog extension (Sep 6)
waves.blurb: The catalog went from 431 foods to 884. You asked for spices first ("cooking isn't just the raw ingredients"), then the thin categories, then everything else a broad probe found missing. Three spec amendments, one PR, one data apply: 117 spices (from 23), 87 plant milks, frozen vegetables and fruit, drinks, fish and shellfish, 186 rows across the twelve families a 267-item probe found half-empty, and 62 more from the advocate's own probe. 223 of them carry a real USDA nutrition panel — every value checked against the federal dataset, none invented. The review also caught something bigger: the Add-tab suggestion list had never searched aliases, and was capped at twenty alphabetical name matches, so 390 new rows pushed Frozen pizza and Peanuts out of their own searches. It now ranks by prefix over the cached, alias-bearing index — typing "haldi" finds Turmeric, "potstickers" finds Dumplings, "seltzer" finds Sparkling water. #200 is the spec for a thirteenth category, Frozen, since frozen peas filed under Produce send you to the wrong aisle; expiry already knew the difference between a freezer and a fridge.

waves.name: Approval wave (Sep 5 evening)
waves.blurb: At 19:40 EDT you approved everything. Merged in dependency order: the skeleton-loading spec (#193) and its three PRs (#196 primitives, timing hook, launch gate, Pantry/Location/Lists; #198 recipes, community, cook mode, folders, creator profile; #197 Profile slots, Item, Expiring, Zones, Insights, Recent, review lists, receipt wait), spec 23 one paid tier (#182), spec 57 email verification (#185), and the USDA nutrition matcher (#156) after its migration 0047 and seed went to production. Each dependent PR was retargeted to main and re-stacked on the squash below it before merging; every merged head had its own green CI run. What to review in depth: the skeleton rules (150 ms delay, 300 ms minimum, Reduce Motion, one announcement), the spec 23 contracts you decided last night (price, trial, welcome grant, lapse), spec 57's strict gate, and spec 45's fail-open nutrition fill on the shelf-life route.

Merged as #194; both rehearsal branches deleted, so only production remains.

The 0055 assert could never pass on any database: it wraps itself in a temporary function whose own body contains the string "neon_auth", then scans every function body for that string and matched itself. Written 2026-09-05, never executed until this rehearsal — which is the whole argument for rehearsing on a branch cut from production. Fixed by excluding temporary schemas, and the fix proved by planting decoy functions in public and app_auth and watching the check still fail on them, so it kept its power rather than being softened into silence.
